titel: Heavy runs: tests and builds through the queue
kurz: Several projects share one PC. If test suites, builds or image runs start at the same time, memory runs out and all of them fail. The AMW therefore puts such runs into one queue for the whole computer – automatically, without an agent having to remember it.
brauchst: Agent folders set up by the AMW (`amw einrichten agenten-ordner <folder>`).
The switch “Send heavy commands through the queue” under Settings › This PC (on by default).

schritte.text: Run `amw einrichten agenten-ordner <folder>` once for every agent folder. This adds the hook; running sessions pick it up after a few seconds.

If an agent starts a heavy command directly (for example the whole test suite), the command is not executed. Instead the agent gets the ready-made replacement: `amw lauf ausfuehren --leicht --beschreibung "Test-Suite" -- <its command>`. It waits until the computer is free, then runs and returns the result. If the same command only appears as quoted text (for example in a message or a commit description) or in a heredoc, this does not apply – only what actually runs is checked; after `cmd /c "…"`, `bash -c '…'`, `iex "…"`, `Start-Process … -ArgumentList "…"`, `start "" "…"` or `& "…"` the content counts as a command.

schritte.titel: Light or heavy – always say which
schritte.text: `--leicht` for normal building and testing: runs in parallel (Settings › This PC › “Light runs at the same time”) and never waits for heavy runs. `--schwer` for AI, graphics card, a window or a lot of memory: runs one at a time. Without either, the AMW rejects the run with this explanation; a recipe brings its own kind. An agent never runs two runs at once – both in the same folder would go wrong.
Under Settings › Project › “More heavy commands”, enter one `Name = pattern` per line, for example `Render maps = maps\.py`.

If you know what a run needs, say so: `--braucht-gb 4` (memory), optionally `--braucht-vram-gb` (graphics memory) and `--braucht-platte-gb` (free disk space). Without it the AMW uses what the same kind of run by the same agent really needed recently (measured, with a margin) – the first time, the project's memory limit. Nobody has to guess.
Overview › control panel › “Computer” shows how many runs are in progress and waiting, and when the computer is expected to be free.

fehler: An agent still starts tests directly
Its folder does not have the hook yet: run `amw einrichten agenten-ordner <folder>`.
A run waits for a long time

The control panel says why: the computer is busy, too little memory is free or a run ahead is waiting – then it also says how much memory that run needs and how much is usable. The human can move a run to the front – with “Move up” in the Computer tile or with `amw lauf vorziehen <nr>`; the run is then at the very front, ahead of every priority level. A lead can only move runs up within their project: ahead of the project's other runs, not ahead of other projects' runs. The list therefore says “moved up by the developer” or “moved up within the project”.
A full run does not count for a release

At its start a run records the commit of the folder its command switches to with `cd`, otherwise of the folder you queue it from. If only a script changes the folder, AMW cannot see it: start the command with `cd /d <folder> &&` or queue it from the worktree it checks. The line “# Stand …” at the top of the output shows the recorded commit.

If a test makes no progress for more than 5 minutes, the full run stops that one test process together with its browser, shows the module and the test as failed (“Zeitgrenze”, time limit) and continues with the remaining modules. A full run ends at the latest after its deadline (default 60 minutes, project setting `gesamtlauf_frist_min`); before that it writes under “Läuft gerade” (running now) which test ran last, and the lead gets a message.
“!! Baum während des Laufs geändert” (tree changed during the run)

Something changed in the checked folder during the full run (a new commit or changed files, except `daten/`), for example because someone built there. The run then ends with FAILED and does not count as evidence. Build in another folder and start the run again.
A single short test is rejected
The pattern is too broad. Single test modules stay free; make your own patterns narrower.
The pattern is not a valid regular expression, for example a bracket is missing.
The computer is idle, but nothing starts

A program outside the queue is using the memory, for example a local AI server or a virtual machine. The control panel shows under “Computer” which program it is, how much it uses and since when. Close it yourself when you no longer need it – the AMW never closes anything.
danach: Heavy by default: whole test suites, browser tests, builds and the split of the web branch.
About runs of another project you only see that the computer is busy and until when – never what is running there.
Every computer has its own queue.
fragen: How does a project get priority?

Under Settings › This PC › “Project priority” you set high, normal or low for each project. Waiting runs then go in this order: first what you moved up yourself, then “high”, then “normal”, then “low” – in order of arrival within a level. A run that is already running is never stopped. The waiting reason names the priority; in the timeline “Computer – today” priority runs are marked with ▲, and the control panel lists them briefly. The setting belongs to the PC, not to a project – you only see the names of other projects on the PC. Within the same level, the project ranking comes next (`amw pc einstellen projekt_rang=AMW,GlassWorld,LayerIT`, only you; projects not listed come after), and only then arrival.
Can a project run heavy jobs only at certain times?

Yes: `amw projekt einstellen lauf_fenster=18:00-07:00` (you or the lead; local time, may span midnight; empty = any time). Heavy runs of this project then start only within that window. Outside it the run shows “wartet auf das Zeitfenster ab 18:00” (waiting for the time window from 18:00) and holds nobody up – other runs move past. Light runs and AI jobs (they have their own AI window) are not affected; a run that is already running is never stopped. On the whole PC only one run at a time uses the graphics card and the screen. So that nothing starves, a waiting run moves up one level for every 30 minutes it waits (adjustable, 0 = off). If two runs end up on the same level this way, the one whose project has that level itself goes first – a real “high” before one that moved up. While a run with “high” waits, another run starts only if enough memory stays free for it afterwards. If it still waits longer than 20 minutes, you get a notice with the reason – only you can move it up. If a run does not fit even with the queue empty, it holds nobody up: the others go past until enough memory is free outside the queue. The same applies to graphics memory: if it is short although no run is using the graphics card, runs with a window go past, and the run starts as soon as enough is free. The waiting reason then says how much the card has, how much is used outside the queue and by which programs – programs the AMW did not start itself are closed only by the human. If less is enough, register the run again with a smaller `--braucht-vram-gb` or without `--gpu`; a note appears right when queuing if it will never fit this way. If a run registered without `--schirm` opens a window anyway, AMW notices: from then on it counts as a run with a window, its agent and the lead are told, and if the screen is taken, the agent is asked to end it (AMW never ends anything itself). For the next 7 days the queue accepts the same run only with `--schirm` – likewise if a run without `--schirm` was closed from outside while the screen was taken. Starting it without a window (for example with `--headless`) counts as a different run. A new console window counts as a window too (for example when a console program is started without a console of its own and Windows opens one for it) – start such programs invisibly, e.g. in PowerShell with `Start-Process … -NoNewWindow` or `-WindowStyle Hidden`. AMW only sees which program has a window, never the window title. **Continuous run:** A long run that is headless and uses no AI, graphics card or window (for example a game simulation) is registered with `--dauerlauf --braucht-gb <GB>`. It runs next to the heavy run, its limit counts towards the reservations (other runs take it into account), and “Computer” shows how much it currently uses. If it uses more than its limit or memory runs short, AMW asks its agent to end it and tells the lead – it does not end it itself.
What happens if the agent's window ends the waiting command?

Nothing is lost. `amw lauf ausfuehren` stores the command, folder and result file when it queues. When the run is due and the waiting command in the window is gone, the service starts exactly this command in the same folder and writes the output to the result file; the agent gets a message with the return code at the end. Runs with a window (screen) are not started by the service.
Does an agent have to watch the queue?

No. “is due” and “runs longer than expected” no longer wake anyone – they only show in the Workbench. Only the result wakes. `amw lauf warte` prints the reason only when it changes. Runs that AMW executes and ends itself (cross-reading, planner, negative test, workers, bundle) send no message at all when they start – only an error at the end is reported.
Why is memory set aside for a running run?

A run often needs its memory bit by bit. So that no second run starts next to it and takes that memory away, the queue keeps its need free. If it did not state a need, the limit of its project applies – but only for the first 15 minutes; after that, what it really uses counts. The waiting reason says how much is set aside for which run.
What happens if the hook fails for once?

Then the command simply runs – an error never blocks anything. The error is written to the log `%LOCALAPPDATA%\amw\hook-fehler.log` on this PC; if there is something in it, have a look, because heavy commands then start directly again.

A program that does not run through the queue and has been using a lot of memory for more than 10 minutes. The AMW only reads the name, memory and start time of the processes – no command lines. Many small processes, such as a browser, do not count.
What does the AMW do when the disk fills up?

It warns: in the control panel under “Computer” and with a message to the lead and you as soon as a drive holding the database or a project folder has less than 15 % free, and urgently below 5 %. Settings › This PC lists the drives and the clean-up suggestions: old backups with size and age. Nothing is deleted automatically. If an archive folder is set, you move old backups there with one click; every move is listed in archiv-protokoll.txt. The AMW also measures the work folders of the Claude sessions (%TEMP%\claude) – per session with agent and project, under Settings › This PC › “Claude work folders”. If a session uses more than 10 GB, its lead and you get a notice. Old working copies in it (folders with .git, unchanged for over a day) are listed with a ready PowerShell command to remove them; the AMW never runs it.
Can I switch this off for one computer?
Yes: Settings › This PC › switch off “Send heavy commands through the queue”. The queue itself stays, only the rejecting stops.
